chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who enters the bathhouse while he is fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who enters the bathhouse while he is fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Does entering a bathhouse invalidate the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that entering the bathhouse (*hammam*) does not break the fast, reflecting the Shia juristic view that mere exposure to heat or water immersion is not inherently invalidating. This ruling underscores the principle of ease (*taysir*) in fasting, distinguishing between physical exertion that causes weakness and simple hygiene practices that preserve the fast's validity.
